title: RequestRevision
description:
Immutable snapshot of a request spec. History and run reports reference
revisions, so editing a request never rewrites past outcomes.

spec_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `spec`.

Id.description: Stable object identifier. UUIDv7 so ids sort roughly by creation time.

RequestSpec.description:
The editable, serializable definition of a request. Execution never
mutates it; a run snapshots it as an immutable [`crate::workspace::RequestRevision`].

source.description: Reference to the imported spec operation this request came from.

Protocol.description:
Wire protocol family of a saved request. SOAP and GraphQL are HTTP body
kinds, not separate transports.

KeyValue.description:
Enabled/disabled name-value entry. Repeated names are legal and preserved
in order (headers and query parameters may repeat).

sensitive.description: Marks the value as sensitive for masking/redaction/export.

Body.description:
Request body model. Serialization (and content-type inference) happens in
the engine before any body-dependent signing.

AttachmentRef.description:
Reference to a content-addressed attachment (binary body, multipart file,
proto file, dataset). The bytes live in encrypted attachment storage or,
for linked files, at a path the user selected on this machine.

oneOf.description: Stored inside Anvil (portable; included in exports).

Linked local file (device-specific; exports report it as a rebinding
requirement rather than copying an absolute machine path silently).

AuthConfig.description:
Auth configuration. Applied after interpolation, content-type inference
and serialization so body-dependent signatures cover the final bytes.

oneOf.description: Use the nearest ancestor folder/workspace auth.
Explicitly send no credentials (clears inherited auth).

signing_key.description: HMAC secret, or PKCS#8 PEM private key for RS/ES algorithms.

oneOf.description: SOAP WS-Security header inserted into the SOAP envelope.

Several explicit presentations in one request (e.g. mTLS + API key).
Order is preserved; conflicting headers fail validation.

SensitiveValue.description:
A field that may carry sensitive material (password, token, key).

* `Template` — text that may contain `{{variable}}` references. A literal
  (non-variable) template in a sensitive field is itself treated as
  sensitive: it is masked in the UI, redacted in history, and replaced by a
  placeholder in safe-share exports.
* `Secret` — a vault reference.

SecretRef.description:
Reference to a value held in the encrypted vault. The value itself never
appears in ordinary object graphs, logs or safe-share exports.

label.description: Human label shown in the UI and in export previews ("prod API key").

KeyLocation.description: Where an API key is presented.

JwtClaims.description:
Claims editor for the JWT helper. Anvil signs only with key material the
user supplies; it never invents an issuer or a gateway token endpoint.

expires_in_secs.description: Lifetime in seconds from signing time; `exp` is computed per send.

not_before_offset_secs.description: `nbf` offset (seconds, may be negative) relative to signing time.

extra_json.description: Additional claims as a JSON object text (may contain `{{vars}}`).

client_secret.description:
Confidential-client secret (client credentials). Public PKCE clients
leave this empty.

client_auth.description: How client credentials are sent to the token endpoint.

token_cache_id.description:
Where the acquired access token is cached (vault) — id of the token
cache entry, managed by the engine.

refresh_skew_secs.description: Refresh this many seconds before expiry.

oneOf.description:
Authorization code with PKCE (S256) through the external system browser
and a loopback redirect bound to one authorization attempt.

namespace.description: Optional namespace bound into the signature when the gateway profile uses one.

allow_unsafe_legacy.description: Explicit opt-in required to use the replayable legacy profile.

HmacProfile.description:
HMAC request signing profile. `FerrumV2` is the gateway's current
single-use profile; `FerrumV1Legacy` is disabled unless the user explicitly
enables the unsafe compatibility option.

oneOf.description: RFC 9530 `Content-Digest: sha-256=:<b64>:`.
Legacy RFC 3230 `Digest: SHA-256=<b64>`.

access_token.description: The access token (bound to the proof key by the issuer).

private_key_pem.description: PKCS#8 PEM of the ES256 proof key (vault reference recommended).

dpop_scheme.description: Present the token as `DPoP <token>` (RFC 9449) or legacy `Bearer`.

handle_nonce_challenge.description: Automatically answer a single `use_dpop_nonce` challenge with a fresh proof.

saml_assertion.description:
User-provided signed SAML assertion XML to embed verbatim (Anvil never
mints assertions).

SettingsOverrides.description:
Non-secret request settings resolved deterministically:
app defaults → workspace → ancestor folders → request → run override.
Every field is optional at each layer; `None` inherits.

HttpVersionPolicy.description: Protocol negotiation policy for HTTP-family requests.

oneOf.description: ALPN negotiation over TLS (h2, then http/1.1); HTTP/1.1 for cleartext.
HTTP/2 over TLS (ALPN `h2` only — fails rather than silently using HTTP/1.1).
Cleartext HTTP/2 with prior knowledge.
Forced HTTP/3 over QUIC. Never silently sends over TCP.
Try HTTP/3 first, then fall back to TCP; every attempt is recorded.

TimeoutOverrides.description: Partial timeout overrides (each class independently inheritable).

forward_credentials_cross_origin.description:
Forward `Authorization`/cookies/client identity to a different origin.
Off by default; the target's own configuration applies otherwise.

RetryPolicy.description:
Automatic retry policy. Off by default. Possibly-processed non-idempotent
operations are never retried automatically regardless of this setting.

only_safe.description:
Retained for compatibility. Retries are always limited to failures
proven `not_dispatched` or idempotent methods; a possibly processed
non-idempotent request is never replayed, whatever this says.

oneOf.description: Operating-system resolver (getaddrinfo).
Query the given DNS servers directly (`ip:port`), bypassing the OS resolver.

addresses.description: Addresses to connect to instead of resolving.

ProxySelection.description: Explicit proxy choice: a profile, or explicitly none (overrides inherited).

max_response_bytes.description:
Hard ceiling on response body bytes read from the wire; exceeded bodies
end with a local `response_too_large` outcome (never a peer fault).

capture_bytes.description:
Bytes retained for display/history; beyond this the body is still read
and counted but marked display-truncated.

Assertion.description:
Declarative, no-code assertion. Assertion failures are reported separately
from transport and application failures.

oneOf.description: Assert the presence/absence of a diagnostic finding code.
Assert transport completion state (`completed`, `failed`, ...).

Extraction.description: Extract a response value into an iteration-local variable for chaining.

sensitive.description: Treat the extracted value as sensitive (masked, redacted from reports).

LintSendPolicy.description:
Policy for sending a body whose syntax lint failed. Anvil is a testing
client, so invalid JSON/XML is sendable by explicit choice.

oneOf.description: Refuse to send until the user chooses "send anyway" for this send.
Warn in the outcome but send.
Do not lint (e.g. deliberate malformed-payload tests).

messages.description: JSON messages to send in order (one for unary / server streaming).

deadline_ms.description: `grpc-timeout` sent to the server, if any.

plaintext.description: Use h2c (cleartext prior knowledge) for `http://` targets.

GrpcSchemaSource.description: Where gRPC message schemas come from.

oneOf.description:
`.proto` sources (compiled in-process; imports resolved only among the
provided files).
Serialized `FileDescriptorSet`.
Server reflection (grpc.reflection.v1, falling back to v1alpha).

messages.description: Messages sent after open (automation / scripted session).

expect_messages.description: Automation: wait for this many inbound messages before closing.

idle_close_ms.description: Close the session after this idle period (automation only).

oneOf.description: RFC 6455 HTTP/1.1 Upgrade.
RFC 8441 Extended CONNECT over HTTP/2.
RFC 9220 Extended CONNECT over HTTP/3.
Hex-encoded bytes.

max_events.description: Stop after this many events (0 = until cancel/idle/max duration).

reconnect.description: Automatic reconnect is off by default; reconnect only when explicitly enabled.

half_close_after_send.description: Half-close (shutdown write) after sending, then keep reading.

expect_frames.description: Stop reading after this many frames (0 = until idle/close/max bytes).

TcpFraming.description:
Framing presets for raw TCP exchanges. Arbitrary bytes are never assumed to
be a known application protocol.

response_window_ms.description: How long to wait for responses after the last datagram is sent.

masque.description:
Send the datagrams through an HTTP/3 MASQUE proxy (RFC 9298
CONNECT-UDP) instead of directly. The request URL stays the UDP
target (`udp://host:port`); the proxy only relays. `None` = direct.

MasqueSpec.description:
RFC 9298 UDP proxying over HTTP/3 ("MASQUE" CONNECT-UDP). Belongs to
the UDP request rather than to a proxy profile: the proxy is addressed by
a URI Template (not `host:port`), carries only UDP, and its datagram
encoding is part of the exchange's evidence (docs/protocols.md).

proxy_url.description:
The proxy's `https://host:port` origin (variables allowed). HTTP/3
needs TLS, so any other scheme is refused before traffic; the TLS
profile setting applies to the QUIC handshake with the proxy.

uri_template.description:
RFC 9298 §2 URI Template path (and optional query) on the proxy.
`{target_host}` and `{target_port}` are expanded from the request URL.

MasqueDatagramMode.description: How HTTP Datagrams (RFC 9297) are carried through the tunnel.

oneOf.description:
QUIC DATAGRAM frames when the proxy's SETTINGS enable HTTP/3
datagrams (`SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM`) and QUIC negotiated DATAGRAM
frames; otherwise DATAGRAM capsules on the CONNECT stream (RFC 9297
§3.5). The encoding used is recorded.

Require QUIC DATAGRAM frames; fail before traffic when the proxy does
not offer HTTP/3 datagrams.
Always DATAGRAM capsules on the CONNECT stream.

ImportSource.description:
Link from a request to the spec/collection it was imported from, used for
reimport diffs.

operation_key.description: Stable key: operationId when present, else `METHOD path`.

generated_hash.description: Hash of the generated request spec at import time (detects user edits).
